reuse.why: The API and planning consumers share getExpectedAmount and reuse getApproxNumberThreshold, but the existing getScheduledAmount retains overlapping dispatch logic.

duplication.why: Most repeated arithmetic is removed, but missing/numeric/range dispatch remains in both amount helpers and schedule-template repeats operator dispatch.

placement.why: Amount policy belongs in shared/schedules, tolerance remains in shared/rules, and API field projection stays in api-models.

scope.why: The edits are confined to schedule amount policy, its consumers, API typing, tests, and release notes.

maintainability.why: Centralizing planning improves ownership, but overlapping amount helpers, caller-side dispatch, and outdated policy comments leave avoidable maintenance ambiguity.

bypasses_abstraction.where: server/budget/schedule-template.ts decides which operators use getExpectedAmount and handles other amounts locally despite the helper supporting that dispatch.

disguised_duplication.where: shared/schedules.ts introduces getExpectedAmount with the missing/numeric/range dispatch already present in getScheduledAmount, reshaped with early returns and without inversion.

abstraction_drift.where: getExpectedAmount introduces the op parameter and isapprox branch; schedule-template.ts retains its own operator gate instead of delegating the complete decision.
